review_evidence: README describes Hale as a Lean 4 port of 45 Haskell libraries with compile-time theorems and type-level invariants across networking, data structures, parsing, concurrency, and web protocols.

Representative library modules define proof-carrying interfaces such as canonical rational numbers with positivity/coprimality invariants, while Tests/Examples.lean contains kernel-checked propositions about those APIs.
The large module and test surface therefore contains reusable definitions, interfaces, and proof witnesses; path roles such as Tests do not satisfy FILTER-004 and no safe exclusion was established.
summary: Retain Hale's full Lean source surface because both library modules and test/example modules contain formal interfaces or checked properties.
